# The Yantra App (`yantra ui`)

`yantra ui` opens Yantra in its own browser window. The window has no address
bar. It is served by a small **app host** process that runs on your computer
and listens only on `127.0.0.1`. You do not need a terminal open to keep using
the window. No other web page or local program can drive it. The app page
loads nothing from anywhere except the host.

The host is a supervisor, not an executor. Every run or change the app starts
runs as an ordinary Yantra command, in its own background process. That process
uses the same handler and arguments a terminal would. Each command starts at
most once. A run keeps going and keeps its data if the window, the host or
both go away.

This release ships the window's frame: a top bar with the Yantra status mark,
a connection banner and a Home page. The queue, run-following, attendance and
artifact behavior described below belongs to the host. The app's screens are
built on it.

## What It Does

### Opens one app host per data directory

- `yantra ui` looks for a running app host for the current data directory. If
  one is running and ready, it is reused. Otherwise `yantra ui` starts one in
  the background and waits up to 10 seconds for it to become ready.
- Two `yantra ui` commands started at the same moment still end up with one
  host. The second one reuses the first one's host.
- `yantra ui` asks the host for a **launch code** and builds the URL
  `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#code=<code>`. A launch code works once, for 60
  seconds. The port is chosen fresh each time a host starts.
- The window removes the code from its address before it does anything else.
  It then exchanges the code for a session (see
  [Privacy and security](#privacy-and-security)).
- If the running host is from a different Yantra version than the CLI you ran,
  `yantra ui` still reuses it. It prints this note on stderr:
  ``The running app is Yantra <old>; close the app and run `yantra ui` to use <new>.``
  The note is not printed with `--json`.

### Chooses the browser that opens the window

`yantra ui` opens the first browser it finds, in this order:

1. **Google Chrome** installed on the system, from the stable, beta, dev or
   canary channel. Chrome for Testing is never used at this step.
2. **Microsoft Edge**, at its standard install locations:
   - Windows: `Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe` under
     `Program Files (x86)`, then under `Program Files`.
   - macOS: `/Applications/Microsoft Edge.app`.
   - Linux: `microsoft-edge` or `microsoft-edge-stable` on `PATH`.
3. **The browser Yantra uses for its own runs**, as `yantra browser` resolves
   it.

Whichever browser is chosen gets the same arguments: `--app=<url>`,
`--user-data-dir=<data-dir>/ui/chrome-profile`, `--no-first-run` and
`--no-default-browser-check`. The window therefore uses its own profile,
separate from your everyday browsing profile and from every automation
profile. It never gets a remote-debugging or automation flag. The browser is
started in the background, and `yantra ui` exits without waiting for it.

If no browser is found, `yantra ui` still prints the URL so that you can open
it yourself, and exits with code 3:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:53817/#code=…
No Chrome, Edge or Yantra browser was found to open the app. Run `yantra browser install`, or open the URL above in Chrome or Edge.
```

### Shows its connection state

A banner under the top bar reports the window's connection to the host. It is
a polite live region, so screen readers announce changes without moving focus.

| State         | What the window shows                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Connecting    | `Connecting to Yantra…`                                                                                                                                  |
| Connected     | No banner. The Home page reads `Connected to the Yantra on this computer.`                                                                               |
| Disconnected  | `Disconnected from Yantra. Reconnecting in <n> s.` (or `Reconnecting…`). Retries back off from 0.5 to 10 seconds, with jitter.                           |
| Session ended | ``Session ended — run `yantra ui` to reopen.`` The page is replaced by **Session ended**: "Run `yantra ui` to reopen the Yantra app."                    |
| Incompatible  | ``This window cannot talk to Yantra <version>. Run `yantra ui` to reopen.`` The page shows **Session ended** with "The running app is Yantra <version>." |

A window's session ends, and the window stops trying to reconnect, when:

- it has been unable to reconnect for 5 minutes;
- the host refuses its credentials, for example because the session expired;
- it was opened 12 hours ago, whether or not it is connected; or
- it was loaded without a usable code, for example a launch URL opened a
  second time or more than 60 seconds after `yantra ui` printed it.

Once a session has ended, only `yantra ui` opens a new window.

**Reloading.** While a window is connected, it fetches a fresh **resume code**
every 45 seconds and keeps it in that tab's `sessionStorage`. A resume code is
single-use and lasts 60 seconds. Pressing F5 exchanges it for a new session for
the same window, and the old session is revoked at that moment. If the tab
cannot use `sessionStorage`, a reload ends the session.

**New app build.** If the page and the host come from different app builds,
the page reloads itself into the host's build. It waits until it is idle:
no request in flight and no text field focused.

### Applies the app appearance preferences

| Preference    | Values                    | Default  | Effect                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ui.theme`    | `system`, `light`, `dark` | `system` | Follow the operating system's light/dark setting, or force one |
| `ui.surfaces` | `glass`, `solid`          | `glass`  | Translucent glass surfaces, or solid surfaces                  |

The window reads the effective values from the same view as
`yantra profile --json`, so a value left at its default or set by hand in
`profile.yaml` also applies. Any unrecognized value falls back to the default.

The window applies the preferences each time it connects. It also applies them
again shortly after `profile.yaml` changes (the host checks every 2 seconds).
`yantra prefs set` stores its value in the preference index, not in
`profile.yaml`, so an open window picks that change up the next time it
connects. Reload the window to apply it at once.

### Shows CLI, daemon and app runs without a reload

While a window is subscribed, the host watches the runs directory and the
history index every 2 seconds. File-system change hints, where available,
trigger an earlier check. Changes are batched for a quarter of a second, then
the host tells the window which runs changed and which runs currently hold a
live lease.

This applies to runs from any source: the terminal, the scheduler daemon or
the app. If file watching is unavailable, the host falls back to polling alone
and logs that once.

### Runs app-started commands as background workers

When the app starts a command, the host does the following:

1. It checks the command line against the same command registry the terminal
   uses.
2. It records the request under `<data-dir>/ui/invocations/`, keyed by an ID
   the window chose.
3. It starts the command, when the queue allows, as a detached `yantra` worker
   process with the host's environment and the request's working directory.

The worker runs exactly what `yantra <command> …` would run in a terminal. A
run started from the app therefore has the usual run directory, lease, run
socket, `run-events.jsonl` and report, and appears in `yantra list` like any
other run.

**Each request starts at most once.** The worker claims its record before it
does anything else. If the window sends the same request ID again, for example
after a lost reply, the host returns the request's current state and never
starts a second worker.

**Some commands never run from the app queue.** The host refuses them and says
where to go instead:

| Kind of command                                                                                  | What the host says                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Reads (`list`, `show`, `audit`, `report`, `prefs list`/`get`, `profile`, …)                      | It is a read; the host answers it directly instead of starting a worker. |
| Commands that handle a secret (`secret set`, `secret list`, `secret rm`)                         | It handles a secret and never runs from the app queue.                   |
| Commands that need an app adapter (such as `init`, `config edit`, `open`, `daemon start`/`stop`) | No adapter is registered yet; run it in a terminal.                      |
| Terminal-only commands (`ui`, `config data-dir`)                                                 | Run `yantra <command>` in a terminal.                                    |

### Queues runs, two at a time

- **Runs** (`ask`, `research`, `do`, `run`, `resume` and other run commands)
  take a slot. At most **two** run at once.
- **Exclusive** commands, such as `browser install` and `browser update`, run
  only when no run is active. While one is active, no new run starts.
- **Commands that only change something** (mutating commands) take no slot and
  start right away.
- Waiting items start strictly in arrival order. An item starts only when it is
  first in line and its slot is free.
- The queue is kept on disk. It survives the window closing and the host
  restarting.

### Asks for review when something changed while queued

When the app submits a command, it records the effective settings and the
workflow or template file contents it showed you. Just before a queued item
starts, the host works those settings out again, without running anything. It
uses the same precedence the worker will use, and re-hashes the files.

If anything differs, the item moves to **needs review** and lists each
difference, with the value you submitted and the current value. A value that
came from an environment variable is shown only by the variable's name, such
as `$YANTRA_AGENT_MODEL`, never by its value. A workflow file that no longer
exists also counts as a difference.

You then choose one of:

- **Use the current values:** the item goes back in the queue as it is.
- **Use the submitted values:** each differing value is added as an explicit
  flag of the command. This choice is unavailable if a workflow or template file
  changed, or if any difference cannot be expressed as a flag of that command.
- **Discard** the item.

### Stops and restarts items

- **Stopping an item that has not started** withdraws it. If a worker was being
  started at that moment, its claim is refused and it exits without doing
  anything.
- **Stopping a started item** asks its run to cancel through the run's socket.
  If the process is still alive after 10 seconds, the host ends that exact
  process tree, identified by creation identity rather than by a bare process
  ID. The run is then reconciled, so it records an outcome.
- **A command with no run** gets the same 10 seconds, and is then ended by
  identity.
- **An item that never started** can be started again at once. Its worker
  provably never ran.
- **An item whose start is unknown** (starting the worker failed partway, so it
  may or may not have run) starts again only after you confirm. The host warns:
  "The earlier start of this item is unknown: it may already have run, so
  starting it again may repeat its effects."

### Survives a window, host or worker going away

| What goes away | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The window     | Runs and the queue continue. The window's session stays valid for 5 minutes after its last connection closes.                                                                                                                                              |
| The host       | Workers keep running. The host never signals a worker when it stops. An open window shows **Disconnected** and cannot reconnect to a new host. Run `yantra ui` again. It starts a new host, which first recovers every request and then resumes the queue. |
| A worker       | Yantra's usual run reconciliation, which also runs when a host starts, ends its run with an `owner_lost` outcome (`partial` or `failed`, from its evidence). The next host start finishes the request with the reason `owner_lost`.                        |

**Recovery on host start** handles each request by its state:

- A request that had not been claimed by its worker becomes **never started**.
  A worker that tries to claim it later is refused.
- A worker that is still alive is left alone. The new host attaches to its run
  as soon as a window follows that run. The window can ask for events from the
  last sequence number it saw, and receives every later event exactly once:
  first from `run-events.jsonl`, then live.
- A worker that has died has its run reconciled, and the request is finished
  as `owner_lost`.
- A worker whose liveness cannot be verified is left unchanged. It is never
  treated as dead.

Queued items are not started by recovery. They start only through the normal
queue, which still runs drift review and the slot check for each one.

**Run following.** If a run's worker speaks an older run-channel version, the
window is told that live updates are unavailable for that run, and the worker
is never stopped. A worker that sends nothing for 30 seconds is reported as not
responding.

**Idle exit.** The host shuts itself down after 10 minutes during which no
window is connected and nothing is queued or starting. Running workers neither
keep it alive nor are touched when it exits. Any window connection or new
request cancels the countdown.

### Counts who is watching (attendance)

A window counts as **attending** only if all three of these hold:

- it is connected;
- it has asked to receive interventions;
- it has checked in within the last 30 seconds. The app checks in every 10
  seconds.

The host sends the number of attending windows to every run it is following.
It sends the number when it changes, when it starts following a run, and every
10 seconds.

**With no window, the count is 0.** A long-running host or a full queue never
counts as someone watching. The host logs only changes in the count. What a run
does with the count is the run's own behavior.

Windows that asked for interventions are also sent each followed run's
`intervention_raised` and `intervention_resolved` events.

## How to Use It

```bash
# Open the app (starts the host if needed)
yantra ui

# Print the URL instead of opening a window
yantra ui --print

# Machine-readable result; still opens the window
yantra ui --json

# Both: print the URL as JSON, open nothing
yantra ui --print --json

# Make the app dark with solid surfaces
yantra prefs set ui.theme dark
yantra prefs set ui.surfaces solid
```

With `--print`, open the URL yourself in a browser on the same computer within
60 seconds. Each `yantra ui --print` issues a new single-use code from the same
host.

To set the appearance by hand, edit `profile.yaml`:

```yaml
ui:
  theme: dark
  surfaces: solid
```

`yantra config set ui.theme …` does not write the setting. It redirects you to
`yantra prefs set ui.theme …`. An invalid value, such as
`yantra prefs set ui.surfaces frosted`, exits with code 1 and lists the valid
values. Only these two `ui.*` keys exist.

## Inputs and Outputs

### `yantra ui` options

| Option    | Effect                                                                    |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--print` | Print the app URL instead of opening a window                             |
| `--json`  | Emit JSON describing the opened app (the URL, too, when no browser opens) |

In human mode a successful open prints `Opened the Yantra app in <browser>.`,
for example `Google Chrome` or `Microsoft Edge`. `--print` prints the URL alone.

### `--json` output

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:53817/#code=…",
  "port": 53817,
  "hostPid": 41236,
  "reused": true
}
```

`reused` is `true` when an already-running host was used. If no browser is
found, the same JSON goes to stdout and the error goes to stderr.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | The window opened, or the URL was printed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `1`  | Invalid usage, such as an unknown option or an extra argument                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `3`  | No browser was found (the URL is still printed); the host lock cannot be verified or read; the host exited before it was ready, or was not ready within 10 seconds (the message names `host.log`); the host could not listen on `127.0.0.1`; the app files are missing ("Rebuild Yantra (pnpm build)."); or the host's control socket was unreachable |

Every exit-3 message ends with one next step. If the host lock is held by a
process whose liveness cannot be verified, the message says:

```text
Close any running Yantra app; if none is running, delete the host.lock file in the data directory's ui folder and run `yantra ui` again.
```

### Files the host keeps

All host files are under `<data-dir>/ui/`, `~/.yantra/data/ui/` by default.
They move with the data directory.

| Path                      | What it is                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host.lock`               | The single-instance record: process identity, port, versions. It never holds a bare process ID |
| `host.log`, `host.log.1`  | The host's own log. It is rotated once at start when it is over 10 MiB                         |
| `host-start-failure.json` | Why the last host start failed, read by `yantra ui`                                            |
| `invocations/`            | One record per app request, plus each worker's result                                          |
| `launch/`                 | The files the host hands to workers                                                            |
| `slots.lock`              | The lock every queue change happens under                                                      |
| `chrome-profile/`         | The app window's own browser profile                                                           |

## Configuration and Permissions

- **Preferences:** `ui.theme` and `ui.surfaces`, described above. Both are
  owned by `yantra prefs`.
- **Environment:** the host captures the environment of the `yantra ui` that
  started it. Workers and drift review use that environment. To change it,
  let the host exit (it stops after 10 idle minutes) and run `yantra ui` from
  the new environment.
- **Data directory:** while the host is running, `yantra config data-dir`
  refuses to relocate. See [Configuration](configuration.md).

### Privacy and security

The host is built for a single user on a single computer.

- **Loopback only.** The host listens on `127.0.0.1`, on a port chosen at
  random, and never on `0.0.0.0`, `::` or `localhost`. It accepts a request
  only if its `Host` header is exactly `127.0.0.1:<port>`; anything else is
  refused with 421, which blocks DNS-rebinding pages.
- **Exact origin.** Every request other than GET or HEAD must carry the exact
  `Origin` `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (403 otherwise). No CORS header is ever
  sent. A page on another local port can neither open a session nor open the
  app's socket.
- **The page talks only to the host.** A strict Content-Security-Policy limits
  the page to its own origin and the host's WebSocket. The end-to-end suite
  checks that the app makes no request beyond `127.0.0.1:<port>` and triggers
  no CSP violation.
- **Sessions.** A window must present all three of these:
  - a single-use launch code, valid for 60 seconds;
  - an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` cookie;
  - a per-window capability that exists only in the page's memory, never in
    storage, the URL or a cookie.

  A cookie from one window combined with another window's capability is
  refused. A capability ends 5 minutes after its window's last connection
  closes, and 12 hours after creation in any case.

- **Never stored or logged.** The host keeps only SHA-256 digests of codes,
  cookies and capabilities, in memory. `host.log` redacts every code, cookie,
  capability, token, signed URL and secret-named field, and the security suite
  checks this with planted canary values.
- **Run files the app can fetch.** The app reaches run files only through
  signed URLs (`/a/…`). A signed URL is bound to one window and lasts 5 minutes.
  Every signed URL stops working when its window's session ends or the host
  restarts.

  Only these run files can be fetched:
  - `report.md`;
  - PNG and JPEG images under `captures/`.

  These are never served, whatever is asked:
  - leases, locks and temporary files;
  - sockets;
  - decision records;
  - the host lock;
  - invocation records;
  - browser profiles.

  A path that escapes the run directory, including through a symbolic link, is
  refused. Anything that is not an image is served as a download rather than
  displayed.

- **No model use in the host.** The host opens no model session. Any agentic
  work happens inside a worker, under the command's usual rules.

## Limitations

- **No exactly-once guarantee for website effects.** The host guarantees that
  each request launches a worker at most once. It cannot guarantee what a run
  did on a website before its worker died. A run that ends `owner_lost` and is
  started again is a new run, and may repeat actions. When a start's outcome is
  unknown, the host asks before starting it again rather than guessing.
- **A window cannot follow a restarted host.** After the host restarts, open a
  new window with `yantra ui`. Its session is new; runs and the queue are
  unaffected.
- **`yantra prefs set` does not reach an open window live.** Reload the window
  to apply it. Edits to `profile.yaml` apply live.
- **Browser discovery is limited** to the locations listed above. A Chrome or
  Edge installed elsewhere is not found. Use `yantra ui --print` and open the
  URL yourself.
- **The launch code is visible in the browser's process arguments**
  (`--app=<url>`). On some systems other local users can read those arguments.
  The code is single-use, lasts 60 seconds, and is spent as soon as the window
  first loads.
- **This release's window has a single Home page.** The host behavior above
  (queue, review, run following, attendance, artifacts) is available to the
  app's screens, but this release adds no screens of its own for it.

For the host's process model and protocol, see
[Architecture](../architecture.md) and the
[Protocol Specification](../protocol-spec.md).
